title: Carry last year's fleet plan into this year's model

blocks.text: A city transit agency re-plans its bus replacements every January. Last year's approved plan, `old_plan`, maps each bus it replaces to a year. This year's model has one binary variable $`x_{b,y}`$ for each bus $`b`$ and each year $`y \in W_b`$ it may now be replaced in, given as `windows[b]`. The year `first_year` has just begun: the replacements planned for it are under way, so they are commitments, not decisions. Some buses are new to the list this year, and some old years are no longer allowed (a supplier moved a delivery).

Before you code, write the rule in this notation: for each $`b`$ and $`y \in W_b`$, what value $`\hat x_{b,y}`$ the start gives, in terms of last year's year $`s_b`$ (when $`b`$ was in the old plan) and the first year $`y_0`$; and which buses form the committed set.

items: `committed(old_plan, first_year)` returns the set of buses last year's plan replaces in `first_year`.

`carry_forward(old_plan, windows, first_year)` returns a complete start: a dict with one value, 1.0 or 0.0, for every `(bus, year)` of `windows`. It keeps last year's decision wherever this year's model can still express it, and gives no other year a 1.

blocks.text: `windows` may still list a committed bus (one replaced in `first_year`), even with `first_year` among its years. That bus is already being replaced, so it is not a decision to hint: the start gives it 0.0 in every year of its window. Only a replacement planned after `first_year` is carried forward as a 1.
The tests call your functions with small plans; no solver runs. About ten lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from fleet import carry_forward, committed

old = {"V1": 2030, "V2": 2032, "V3": 2031, "V4": 2034}
windows = {"V2": [2031, 2032], "V3": [2031, 2032, 2033], "V4": [2031, 2032], "V7": [2031]}

print("committed in 2030:", committed(old, 2030))
start = carry_forward(old, windows, 2030)
for key, value in start.items():
    print(f"start for {key}:", value)

cases.says: a bus whose old year is still allowed is hinted 1 in that year and 0 in its other years
the buses planned for the year that has begun are committed
every variable of this cycle gets a value, zeros included
a bus that was not in last year's plan has no year to carry
an old year that is no longer allowed is dropped, not moved to another year
a replacement in the year that has begun is committed, so it is not hinted

origin.section: Last Cycle's Plan Must Be Mapped Onto This Cycle's Variables

concepts: a rolling plan commits its first year and slides the horizon, so last cycle's decisions map onto this cycle's variables or nowhere
